compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090M Blackwell sm_100, 82 SMs, 128KB smem/SM, FP16 TC 210TF (FP32 accum). Output H'=360,W'=640. 32 out-channels * 16 in-channels * 9 = 4608 FP16 weights = 9KB easily fits in shared/constant.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv 3x3 with C_in=16, C_out=32 is small GEMM-like; output spatial dominates work. Per-output FLOPs = 2*16*9 = 288 multiply-adds. Total ops ~ 32*720*1280*288 = 8.5 GFLOPs (small), so memory/launch dominate. ReLU+AvgPool fuse trivially.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Tensor Core utilization may be hard given small K=144 and tile shapes; epilogue fusion required.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input 1*16*720*1280*2B = 29.5MB (fits in L2=64MB). Output (after pool) 1*32*360*640*2B = 14.7MB. Weights 9KB. Memory bound likely; fusing conv+relu+avgpool removes intermediate 1*32*720*1280*2B=59MB traffic.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Without fusion, intermediate write/read dominates; with fusion, input reuse across pool 2x2 must be exploited.

register_pressure.notes: Per-thread storing multiple output pixels and partial sums for 32 channels could push register usage; need tile sizing.
register_pressure.risk: Spilling if each thread computes all 32 out-channels for a 2x2 block (32*4 accumulators).

nodes.notes: 1) Classification: fused stencil (3x3 conv) + elementwise (ReLU) + reduction (2x2 avgpool). Dense, no indirection. Fixed small shapes: N=1,Cin=16,Cout=32,H=720,W=1280,K=3,P=1,pool=2. 2) Math: out[c,y,x] = avg over 2x2 of relu(sum_{ic,ky,kx} in[ic,2y+ky-0..,2x+kx-0..]*W[c,ic,ky,kx]+b[c]). Output spatial 360x640. Each output reads a 5x5 input patch per in-channel (16 channels) -> 16*5*5=400 input FP16 reads = 800B. 3) Layout: NCHW FP16 contiguous; weights small (9KB) -> constant/shared; bias 64B. 4) Regimes: (a) memory-bound input read (most likely given small compute), (b) register-bound if accumulating all 32 outc per thread, (c) launch/occupancy bound if too few blocks. 5) Knobs: tile shape (output tile HxW), per-thread output pixels, shared mem for input halo, weights in smem vs constant, FP16 vs FP32 accumulate, vectorized __half2 loads, tensor cores (im2col-like reshape -> GEMM Cout=32 x (Hout*Wout)=460800 x K=144). 6) Skeleton: grid over output tile (e.g., 16x16 output pixels = 32x32 input region per Cin); load input tile to smem cooperatively; each thread computes a small output block over all 32 Cout, applies bias+ReLU; reduce across 2x2 pool inline; write out. 7) Candidates: F1 (TOP) fully-fused direct conv kernel with shared-mem input tile + constant weights + inline ReLU+AvgPool, one kernel call, no intermediate global. F2 implicit-GEMM with tensor cores (Cout=32 fits one m16n8 tile of N=8, but K=144=9*16 well-suited). F3 split kernels (rejected: 59MB intermediate). Working set per block: input tile ~ (Tile_H*2+2)*(Tile_W*2+2)*16*2B; for tile 16x16 -> 34*34*32B = 36KB fits in 128KB smem easily. Full fusion is register-feasible -> F1 is top.

action.description: Single fused CUDA kernel: each block computes a tile of output pixels (e.g., 16x16 = covers 32x32 input region for Cin=16). Cooperatively load input halo (34x34x16 FP16) into shared memory. Store all 32*16*9 = 4608 FP16 weights in __constant__ memory or shared. Each thread computes a small block of output pixels across all 32 output channels using FP16 accumulation in registers (or FP32 for safety). Apply bias + ReLU, then perform 2x2 average inline (each thread group reduces 4 conv outputs into one pooled output). Write final pooled output directly to global memory. Eliminates intermediate Cout*H*W tensor.
action.rationale: Reference likely runs unfused conv->relu->pool with large intermediate. Full fusion removes ~59MB of intermediate traffic and exploits input reuse across the 2x2 pool window.
action.title: Fully-fused Conv3x3+ReLU+AvgPool2x2 direct kernel with smem input tile + constant weights

memory_bandwidth.notes: Removes intermediate 59MB write+read. Net DRAM traffic ~ input (29.5MB) + output (14.7MB) + weights (9KB) ~= 44MB. At 896GB/s peak -> ~0.05ms theoretical lower bound.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If smem bank conflicts or non-coalesced loads occur, BW gain reduced.

register_pressure.notes: If each thread computes 2x2 pooled output across all 32 Cout -> 32 accumulators (FP16) or 32 FP32 = manageable. With 4 pool outputs collapsed per thread, accumulate then average.
register_pressure.risk: FP32 accum * 32 channels = 128B/thread regs; combined with input staging could hit limit at 128 threads/block.

nodes.notes: CURRENT: does: Fused Conv3x3+ReLU+AvgPool2x2 in single kernel; each thread computes 2x2 conv outputs then pools to 1 output pixel; weights/bias in constant mem; input tile staged in shared memory. bottleneck: compute/register pressure -- the inner loop accumulates over COUT*CIN with 4 accumulators per thread and converts FP16->FP32 each time; no tensor cores used. FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent: yes. UPDATE_BELIEF: 7.43x speedup vs reference (0.432ms vs 3.210ms) confirms fusion + smem tiling + constant weights is a strong design. Next bet: refinements as children -- (a) use HMMA tensor cores on the per-output-channel reduction or vectorized half2 FMA to halve math ops, (b) hoist input patch/weights into registers once and reuse across oc loop, (c) reorder loops so smem input is read once per (c, patch) and accumulate into a register array of size COUT. impacts: memory_bandwidth rating 8/10 (intermediate eliminated, input loaded once via smem); register_pressure rating 5/10 (4 accumulators + patch[4][4] + wf[9] per inner iter -- moderate); compute rating 6/10 (scalar FP32 FMA, no tensor cores).

action.description: Reformulate conv as implicit GEMM: M=Cout=32, N=Hout*Wout per tile, K=Cin*9=144. Use FP16 tensor cores (m16n8k16) with FP16 accumulation (420 TFLOPS path) or FP32 accum (210 TFLOPS). Fuse ReLU+AvgPool in epilogue: write only after 2x2 reduction. Use ldmatrix + cp.async for input staging. Cout=32 -> 2 warps along M; tile N along output spatial.
action.rationale: Tensor cores offer high throughput but problem is memory-bound; gain may be modest. Worth trying if direct kernel is compute-limited at small tile sizes.

kernel_summary: Fused stencil+elementwise+reduction pipeline: 3x3 Conv2d (Cin=16, Cout=32, pad=1, stride=1) followed by ReLU and 2x2 AvgPool, on a 1x16x720x1280 FP16 NCHW input producing 1x32x360x640 FP16 output. Compute is tiny (~8.5 GFLOPs) so the kernel is memory-bound; weights are only 9KB (fit in constant/shared). The dominant optimization is fusing all three ops into a single kernel to eliminate the 59MB intermediate tensor between Conv+ReLU and AvgPool. Each block should load a halo'd input tile into shared memory once and produce pooled outputs directly. FP16 precision with tolerance rtol=atol=0.01 permits FP16 or FP32 accumulation.
open_questions: What is the reference kernel's measured latency, and is it already fused or a naive 3-pass pipeline?
What input/output tile shape best balances smem usage (input halo ~ (2T+2)^2 * Cin * 2B) and occupancy on sm_100?
Is FP16 accumulation accurate enough for Cin*K*K=144 MACs within rtol/atol=0.01, or is FP32 accumulation required?
Should weights live in __constant__ memory (broadcast-friendly) or shared memory (more bandwidth)?
Does NCHW direct convolution beat an NHWC tensor-core implicit-GEMM here given the memory-bound regime?
Can __half2 vectorized loads be used safely given padding boundaries and odd row alignment?
Is there bias to apply (Conv2d bias=True in reference) - confirm exact epilogue order: bias -> ReLU -> avg of 4?
Are there any cudaStream / persistent-kernel considerations, or is a single straight launch sufficient?
